relevance_note: Registry survey of 36 children with LAD (CD18-deficient) given HSCT, with per-patient transplant rows in Tables 1 and 2: "The course of 36 children with a confirmed diagnosis of LAD who underwent HSCT between 1993 and 2007 was retrospectively analysed."
method_note: Tables 1 (27 survivors) and 2 (9 deaths) were transcribed by a short Python script from the Markdown rows and checked against the tables by eye; the first column of both tables is an unheaded bare-number patient index, so labels are 'Table 1 #k' and 'Table 2 #k' (the text's 'patients no 2 and 22' refers to Table 1 RIC patients; the Table 1 labels were kept to avoid clashing with Table 2's numbering). No ITGB2 variant, gene name or genotype is given for any patient, so the variants table is empty; diagnosis was by reduced/absent CD18 expression (inclusion criterion, used only for clinical_diagnosis_basis, not for features). The paper says 'LAD' (Introduction: 'LAD type 1'); all patients are treated as LAD-I in scope. Phenotypic rows are post-transplant findings: Table 1 'Gvhd' grade and 'Infections' column (one row per listed agent; 'Pneumonit is' is a split word recorded as 'Pneumonitis'; 'Crypto' undefined and not mapped), and Table 2 'GVHD Grade' and 'Cause of death' terms. Checklist 'fungal infections' observed for Table 1 #19 ('Fungal'), #23 and #27 ('Candida'); everything else not reported (empty cells are not reported; no symbol is defined as absent). Age columns are age at transplant (in treatment_summary), not onset, diagnosis or last evaluation; age at last evaluation and age at death were not computed. Contradiction: the text says the 9 deaths were '4 haploidentical, 3 sibling donor and 2 matched unrelated donor', but Table 2 shows 3 MSD, 1 MUD and 5 rows with no donor; donor was left as printed. Table 1 rows 24-27 and Table 2 rows 5-9 have blank donor/conditioning/graft cells (presumably haploidentical, not stated) and were not filled. No statement that any patient was described in an earlier publication (refs 10-15 are other transplant reports, not linked to these patients).
